mechanism: Dexamethasone enhances renal potassium and magnesium wasting while chlorthalidone causes similar electrolyte depletion, resulting in additive hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia; both drugs can also cause hyperglycemia and fluid retention effects are opposing.
action: Monitor serum potassium, magnesium, and glucose regularly; consider potassium supplementation or concurrent potassium-sparing agent; assess blood pressure control as dexamethasone may antagonize chlorthalidone's antihypertensive effect.
